item.title: Contratto di ricerca: Sviluppo di detector a cascata quantica basati su Ge/SiGe quantum wells per fotonica integrata nel medio infrarosso - 2026_CDR_DFIS_9 (Politecnico MILANO)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-03 12:00
Institution: Politecnico MILANO, Milan
Field: Physics / 02/PHYS-03 Fisica sperimentale della materia e applicazioni

The research activities are in the framework of the MIDSENSE project. MIDSENSE aims to develop and experimentally validate a fully integrated mid-infrared (MIR) sensing platform based entirely on silicon-compatible photonics technologies. The core objective is the realization of Ge/SiGe Quantum Cascade Detectors (QCDs)[1,2] monolithically integrated within silicon photonic circuits to enable compact, scalable, and low-noise molecular sensing systems operating in the MIR fingerprint region.

item.title: Contratto di ricerca: Cryogenic charged-particle detector for space telescopes (Univ. GENOVA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-03 23:59
Institution: Univ. GENOVA, Genova
Field: Physics / 02/PHYS-01 Fisica sperimentale delle interazioni fondamentali e applicazioni

Space telescopes designed to observe the distant universe and low-intensity sources require anticoincidence detectors to suppress noise caused by cosmic rays. The project entails developing micromachined silicon detectors featuring superconducting Transition-Edge Sensors (TES) designed for operation at the telescope's focal plane temperature of 50 mK. Specifically, this project is part of the detector development for the European Space Agency’s future X-ray astrophysics telescope, newATHENA, under the coordination of the Italian Space Agency. item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-08 23:59
Institution: Univ. Bocconi MILANO, Milano
Field: Physics / 02/PHYS-02 Fisica teorica delle interazioni fondamentali, modelli, metodi matematici e applicazioni

The project aims to develop and validate learning rules that are local in space and time for recurrent neural networks, based on the geometry of stable states and compatible with low-power neuromorphic processors. Activities include theoretical analysis for continuous and finite-precision units, convergence analysis, assessment of scalability and performance in online, continual and few-shot learning, quantization of weights and activations, and validation on emulators and physical hardware.
